assumptions: subdomain of evidence_synthesis_and_systematic_review; nodes are concrete evaluable work units of evidence grading and appraisal
GRADE is the primary certainty framework; OCEBM levels are referenced as an alternative hierarchy
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
grading is performed per prioritized outcome, not per body of evidence
intervention reviews are the default; qualitative and prognostic variants handled via dedicated nodes
exclusions: search strategy design and study screening
data extraction and statistical meta-analysis mechanics (used as inputs only)
primary-study conduct and reporting standards (CONSORT/STROBE) beyond appraisal use
guideline implementation and dissemination after recommendation issuance

competency_questions.question: Given a review question and decision context, what scope and prioritized outcome set must be fixed before any grading begins?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_PICO_FRAME fixes PICO and prioritized outcomes

competency_questions.question: Given a study's design, what starting level of certainty and level-of-evidence anchor applies?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVIDENCE_HIERARCHY maps design to starting anchor

competency_questions.question: How does certainty move up or down from its starting anchor to a final per-outcome rating?
Which risk-of-bias tool applies to a randomized vs a non-randomized study, and at what unit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROB2_RCT and ROBINS_I_NRSI route by design at per-result unit

competency_questions.question: How are per-study risk-of-bias judgments reconciled and aggregated into the GRADE risk-of-bias domain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DUAL_ASSESSOR_RECONCILE and RISK_OF_BIAS_DOMAIN describe reconciliation and aggregation

competency_questions.question: Which design-specific quality-appraisal instrument and tool version applies to each included study or review?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QA_APPRAISAL_TOOLS and TOOL_VERSION_GOVERNANCE map tools and versions

competency_questions.question: What are the five GRADE downgrading domains and what evidence triggers each downgrade?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: the five domain nodes define triggers

competency_questions.question: How do funding sources and publication-bias signals modulate trust in the body of evidence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COI_FUNDING_APPRAISAL and PUBLICATION_BIAS_DOMAIN cover sponsorship and missing-study bias

competency_questions.question: How is recommendation strength derived from certainty without conflating the two?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECOMMENDATION_STRENGTH uses EtD factors, decoupled from CERTAINTY_INTEGRATION

competency_questions.question: How is each certainty rating made auditable and traceable to its domain rationale and sources?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVIDENCE_PROFILE_TRACE and CERTAINTY_INTEGRATION provide the audit trail

competency_questions.question: How are per-outcome effects and certainty presented for decision-makers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SOF_TABLE and RECOMMENDATION_STRENGTH present effects, certainty, and strength

competency_questions.question: How is applicability/indirectness to the decision context assessed against the frozen question?
How is confidence in qualitative evidence assessed distinctly from quantitative certainty?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CERQUAL_QUAL applies the four CERQual components

competency_questions.question: When and how are certainty ratings re-graded as new evidence, disclosures, or guidance emerge?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UPDATING_SURVEILLANCE, COI_FUNDING_APPRAISAL, and TOOL_VERSION_GOVERNANCE define re-grade triggers

glossary.definition: GRADE rating (high/moderate/low/very low) of how much we can trust an effect estimate for an outcome
extent to which study design/conduct features may distort an effect estimate
Cochrane per-result risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials, five domains, algorithmic overall judgment
per-result risk-of-bias tool for non-randomized studies of interventions, seven domains, target-trial framed
critical appraisal tool rating confidence in the conduct of a systematic review
lowering certainty from its starting anchor due to one of the five GRADE domains
raising certainty (typically of NRSI) for large effect, dose-response, or opposing residual confounding
GRADE table presenting per-outcome effects, participant counts, and certainty
detailed GRADE table tracing each certainty judgment to its domain rationale
framework for confidence in findings from qualitative evidence syntheses
GRADE classification of a recommendation as strong or conditional based on EtD factors
degree to which the body of evidence differs from the PICO question (population, intervention, comparator, outcome)
wide confidence interval relative to a decision threshold or insufficient information size
distortion from selectively unpublished or missing studies

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established evidence-grading and appraisal literature (e.g., Higgins et al. Cochrane Handbook 2019; Gough, Oliver & Thomas Introduction to Systematic Reviews 2017; GRADE Working Group guidance; RoB2/ROBINS-I/AMSTAR-2/CERQual method papers) and standard practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix the appraisal scope, PICO/PECO elements, and the certainty-bearing outcomes before any grading or risk-of-bias work begins.
contradictors: narrative reviewer who grades without a fixed question

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: scope or outcome set changes after grading has started

pros.claim: Certainty is graded per outcome, so a fixed prioritized outcome set is the unit of all downstream grading
pros.example: critical outcome 'all-cause mortality' graded separately from surrogate 'LDL change'

pros.claim: Anchoring the decision context (guideline vs descriptive) sets whether recommendation strength is even in scope
pros.example: a descriptive review fixes EtD/strength as out of scope upfront

cons.claim: Over-narrow outcome prioritization can drop outcomes that drive the recommendation
cons.example: omitting harms outcomes biases the net-benefit grade

cons.claim: PICO rigidity can mismatch real-world heterogeneity of included studies
cons.example: broad population PICO forces inconsistency downgrades later

failure_modes: grading the body of evidence rather than per-outcome
surrogate outcomes treated as critical without justification
acceptance_tests: each critical/important outcome has an explicit importance rating
unit of grading is per-outcome and documented
decision context (recommendation in/out of scope) is recorded
revisit_triggers: decision context shifts from descriptive to recommendation

nodes.definition: Map each included study to its design-based starting level of evidence and its initial GRADE certainty anchor (RCT=high, NRSI=low) under the chosen hierarchy.
contradictors: hierarchy-skeptic who weights all designs equally
inputs: included study list with design labels

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: study reclassified between RCT and NRSI designs

pros.claim: Design-based starting anchor is the entry point for all subsequent GRADE up/down movement
pros.example: cluster-RCT starts high; cohort starts low before upgrade factors

pros.claim: Explicit hierarchy choice (GRADE vs OCEBM) prevents silent scheme mixing
pros.example: declaring GRADE precludes citing OCEBM 'Level 2b' in the same SoF

cons.claim: Rigid hierarchies can undervalue strong NRSI with large effects
cons.example: a high-quality cohort with RR 5 is undervalued at 'low' start

cons.claim: Design labels in source papers are often misreported
cons.example: 'prospective cohort' labelled but actually cross-sectional

failure_modes: mixing two incompatible level schemes in one review
starting NRSI at 'moderate' without justification
acceptance_tests: every included study has one design classification
starting certainty anchor recorded per design per outcome
revisit_triggers: new study designs added to the body of evidence

nodes.definition: Apply the Cochrane RoB2 tool per-result to randomized trials across its five domains and derive an overall risk-of-bias judgment.

excluded: certainty downgrading decision (uses this as input)

contradictors: reviewer using legacy RoB1 summary-assessment-by-study

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: RoB2 algorithm/signalling guidance updated or new trial protocol obtained

pros.claim: Per-result, domain-based, algorithm-driven judgments are reproducible and feed the GRADE risk-of-bias domain
pros.example: intention-to-treat effect graded separately from per-protocol

pros.claim: Signalling questions reduce assessor latitude vs global gestalt judgments
pros.example: 'low/some-concerns/high' derived by algorithm not opinion

cons.claim: RoB2 is labor-intensive and per-result, multiplying assessments
cons.example: one trial with 4 outcomes needs up to 4 RoB2 assessments

cons.claim: Domain-to-overall algorithm can feel mechanistic for borderline trials
cons.example: 'some concerns' in one domain forces non-low overall

failure_modes: assessing per-study instead of per-result
ignoring deviations-from-intervention domain for effect of assignment vs adherence
acceptance_tests: each domain has a signalling-question-supported judgment
overall judgment follows the RoB2 algorithm
revisit_triggers: new trial registration or protocol surfaces
outcome added requiring new per-result assessment

nodes.definition: Apply ROBINS-I per-result to non-randomized studies of interventions across its seven bias domains against an explicit target trial.
contradictors: reviewer applying Newcastle-Ottawa only to NRSI for grading

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: confounder list revised or target-trial definition changed

pros.claim: Target-trial anchoring makes confounding and selection bias assessable against a causal benchmark
pros.example: compares cohort to the hypothetical RCT it emulates

pros.claim: Seven-domain structure captures NRSI-specific biases RCT tools miss
pros.example: baseline confounding domain has no RoB2 analogue

cons.claim: Confounding judgment depends on a prespecified confounder list that is often incomplete
cons.example: unmeasured confounder omitted yields false 'moderate'

cons.claim: 'Critical' rating effectively excludes a study from synthesis, a high-stakes call
cons.example: a single critical domain caps overall at critical

failure_modes: scoring like Newcastle-Ottawa stars instead of domain judgments
omitting a key confounder from the prespecified list
acceptance_tests: prespecified confounder list exists before assessment
each domain judged against the target trial
overall judgment uses the worst-domain logic
revisit_triggers: NRSI added to body of evidence

nodes.definition: Select and apply the design-appropriate quality-appraisal instrument (Newcastle-Ottawa, JBI checklists, AMSTAR-2 for included reviews) distinct from GRADE certainty.
contradictors: reviewer who treats an appraisal score as a certainty grade
outputs: AMSTAR-2 confidence ratings for included reviews

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: tool versions revised (e.g., AMSTAR-2 critical-domain set updated)

pros.claim: Design-matched checklists capture quality dimensions RoB tools omit and support umbrella reviews
pros.example: AMSTAR-2 flags absent protocol in an included review

pros.claim: JBI/NOS provide pragmatic appraisal where RoB2/ROBINS-I are too heavy
pros.example: prevalence study appraised with JBI checklist

cons.claim: Appraisal scores (e.g., NOS stars) are routinely misused as bias certainty
cons.example: NOS 7/9 mis-read as 'low risk of bias'

cons.claim: Tool proliferation creates inconsistency across the review
cons.example: two appraisers pick different JBI vs NOS for the same design

failure_modes: summing checklist items into a single threshold score for grading
using NOS in place of ROBINS-I for certainty
acceptance_tests: each design mapped to exactly one appraisal tool
appraisal outputs kept distinct from GRADE certainty
AMSTAR-2 critical domains flagged for included reviews

nodes.definition: Aggregate per-study RoB2/ROBINS-I results into the GRADE study-limitations (risk-of-bias) domain and decide downgrade magnitude for each outcome.

included: weighting by study contribution to the estimate
downgrade by one or two levels

contradictors: grader who downgrades from the worst single study regardless of weight

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: study weights change after re-meta-analysis or new study inclusion

pros.claim: Weighting by contribution to the pooled estimate prevents over-downgrading on low-weight flawed studies
pros.example: a high-RoB study with 2% weight does not force a downgrade

pros.claim: Restriction-to-low-RoB sensitivity analysis tests robustness of the rating
pros.example: estimate stable when high-RoB trials removed

cons.claim: Choosing one vs two-level downgrade is judgment-heavy and weakly specified
cons.example: borderline 'serious' vs 'very serious' RoB

cons.claim: Aggregation can mask a single dominant flawed study
cons.example: one large high-RoB trial drives both estimate and bias

failure_modes: double-counting RoB by also downgrading via imprecision
ignoring weight and downgrading on worst study
acceptance_tests: downgrade justified against weighted study contributions
sensitivity analysis restricting to low RoB is reported or justified absent

nodes.definition: Assess unexplained heterogeneity across study results and decide certainty downgrading for inconsistency for each outcome.
contradictors: grader who downgrades on I-squared alone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new studies change the heterogeneity pattern

pros.claim: Combining point-estimate spread, CI overlap, and I-squared avoids single-statistic errors
pros.example: wide CIs that overlap need not be downgraded

pros.claim: Explained heterogeneity (via subgroups) can avoid an unnecessary downgrade
pros.example: heterogeneity fully explained by dose subgroup

cons.claim: I-squared is sample-size sensitive and easily over-interpreted
cons.example: high I-squared with trivial absolute differences

cons.claim: Post-hoc subgroup 'explanations' can mask real inconsistency
cons.example: data-dredged subgroup rescues a spurious estimate

failure_modes: mechanical I-squared thresholds (>50% = downgrade)
ignoring direction-of-effect inconsistency
acceptance_tests: inconsistency judged on multiple heterogeneity signals not I-squared alone
subgroup explanations are prespecified or flagged post-hoc

nodes.definition: Assess how far the body of evidence's population, intervention, comparator, and outcomes deviate from the PICO question and decide downgrading for indirectness.
contradictors: grader who ignores surrogate-outcome indirectness

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: decision-context population diverges from study populations

pros.claim: Surrogate-outcome detection prevents over-certainty on patient-important effects
pros.example: downgrades certainty when only LDL, not events, measured

pros.claim: Explicit PICO-match scoring makes applicability auditable
pros.example: records that study comparator differs from standard care

cons.claim: Indirectness judgments are subjective and content-knowledge dependent
cons.example: experts disagree on whether a comparator is 'too different'

cons.claim: Easy to conflate with inconsistency or imprecision
cons.example: penalizing the same gap twice across domains

failure_modes: ignoring indirect (network) comparisons
not flagging surrogate outcomes as indirect
acceptance_tests: each PICO element checked against included studies
revisit_triggers: new studies with different populations added

nodes.definition: Assess whether the confidence interval around the pooled effect is wide enough to cross a decision threshold and decide downgrading for imprecision.
contradictors: grader who uses statistical significance as the precision test

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new data narrows or widens the pooled CI

pros.claim: Threshold-based (MID) precision is decision-relevant, not just statistical
pros.example: CI excludes MID so no downgrade despite non-significance

pros.claim: OIS guards against under-powered bodies of evidence being called precise
pros.example: few events trigger imprecision downgrade

cons.claim: Choosing the MID/decision threshold is contested and value-laden
cons.example: different MIDs flip the downgrade decision

cons.claim: Single-study bodies make OIS hard to assess
cons.example: one small trial yields an unstable CI

failure_modes: using p<0.05 instead of CI-vs-threshold
ignoring OIS for rare-event outcomes
acceptance_tests: precision judged against an explicit decision threshold/MID

nodes.definition: Assess the risk that the body of evidence is missing studies (small-study/publication bias) and decide downgrading for publication bias.
contradictors: grader who relies on funnel plots with under 10 studies

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: trial registry reveals unpublished completed studies

pros.claim: Registry/grey-literature comparison detects missing-study bias beyond funnel plots
pros.example: registered-but-unpublished trials flagged

pros.claim: Sponsorship-pattern review links to funding/COI appraisal
pros.example: all positive trials are industry-funded

cons.claim: Funnel-plot tests are unreliable with few or heterogeneous studies
cons.example: asymmetry from heterogeneity mistaken for bias

cons.claim: Publication bias is often suspected but rarely provable
cons.example: downgrade rests on indirect signals

failure_modes: funnel plot with <10 studies treated as definitive
ignoring registries entirely
acceptance_tests: small-study assessment only when study count adequate
registry comparison performed or justified absent

nodes.definition: Decide whether large effect, dose-response, or plausible-confounding-toward-null factors justify upgrading certainty for (typically) non-randomized evidence.
contradictors: grader who upgrades RCT evidence already at high certainty

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: effect magnitude or dose-response evidence changes

pros.claim: Upgrade factors rescue strong NRSI from automatic 'low', balancing the hierarchy
pros.example: RR 6 with dose-response upgrades cohort certainty

pros.claim: Plausible-confounding-toward-null logic strengthens causal claims
pros.example: confounding would shrink, not inflate, the observed effect

cons.claim: Upgrading only applies when no serious downgrade flags exist, easy to misapply
cons.example: upgrading a study already serious for RoB

cons.claim: Large-effect thresholds (RR>2) are conventions, not laws
cons.example: borderline RR 1.9 disputes

failure_modes: upgrading evidence that has unresolved downgrade flags
upgrading RCT bodies already at high
acceptance_tests: upgrade applied only when no serious downgrades remain
each upgrade factor justified with data
revisit_triggers: effect magnitude changes with new data

nodes.definition: Integrate starting level, all downgrade domains, and any upgrades into a single overall GRADE certainty rating (high/moderate/low/very low) per outcome.
contradictors: grader who averages domain scores numerically

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any constituent domain rating changes

pros.claim: Single per-outcome certainty rating is the primary deliverable feeding SoF and recommendations
pros.example: 'moderate certainty for mortality' anchors the recommendation

pros.claim: Explicit integration audit trail makes the rating reproducible and contestable
pros.example: records each level dropped and why

cons.claim: Integration is non-additive judgment; equal domain concerns can sum differently
cons.example: two 'serious' flags may drop one or two levels

cons.claim: Double-counting across correlated domains is a persistent risk
cons.example: RoB and imprecision both penalize the same small trials

failure_modes: numerically averaging domains
dropping below very-low or above high (floor/ceiling violation)
acceptance_tests: no domain double-counted in the integration trail
upgrades applied only after downgrade resolution

nodes.definition: Construct GRADE Summary-of-Findings tables presenting per-outcome absolute/relative effects, participant counts, certainty, and plain-language statements.
contradictors: author who omits absolute effects

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: certainty ratings or effect estimates revised

pros.claim: Absolute effects plus certainty make findings interpretable for decision-makers
pros.example: NNT and certainty shown together per outcome

pros.claim: Standardized footnotes tie each downgrade to its certainty domain
pros.example: footnote: 'downgraded for risk of bias'

cons.claim: Tables can imply more precision than the certainty warrants
cons.example: crisp numbers next to 'very low' certainty mislead

cons.claim: Baseline-risk assumptions drive absolute effects and are often arbitrary
cons.example: wrong assumed control risk distorts the SoF

failure_modes: presenting relative effects only
footnotes not linked to the certainty domain that caused the downgrade
acceptance_tests: each outcome shows absolute and relative effect with certainty
every downgrade has a domain-linked footnote

nodes.definition: Assess confidence in qualitative-evidence-synthesis findings using GRADE-CERQual's four components (methodological limitations, coherence, adequacy, relevance).
contradictors: reviewer applying quantitative GRADE to qualitative findings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: qualitative findings or component judgments revised

pros.claim: CERQual provides a transparent confidence framework for qualitative findings parallel to GRADE
pros.example: each finding rated high/moderate/low/very-low confidence

pros.claim: Separates qualitative confidence from quantitative certainty to avoid mis-grading
pros.example: prevents I-squared logic on themes

cons.claim: Adequacy and relevance judgments are interpretive and reviewer-dependent
cons.example: sparse data adequacy disputed

cons.claim: Less established/validated than quantitative GRADE
cons.example: fewer worked examples for novel domains

failure_modes: applying quantitative downgrade domains to themes
ignoring the relevance component
acceptance_tests: each finding rated on all four CERQual components
quantitative GRADE domains not applied to themes

nodes.definition: Appraise funding sources and conflicts of interest at study and review level and decide how they modulate trust in the body of evidence.
contradictors: reviewer who treats funding as irrelevant to evidence trust

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: undisclosed sponsorship or COI later revealed

pros.claim: Funding/COI appraisal contextualizes RoB and publication-bias domains
pros.example: industry-funded positive results trigger closer scrutiny

pros.claim: Reviewer-COI management protects the appraisal's own credibility
pros.example: COI'd assessors recused from grading their own trials

cons.claim: GRADE has no dedicated funding domain, so placement is ambiguous
cons.example: funding concern split awkwardly across RoB/pub-bias

cons.claim: Disclosures are self-reported and often incomplete
cons.example: undisclosed advisory-board payments

failure_modes: double-penalizing funding under multiple domains
ignoring reviewer COI in the grading team
acceptance_tests: funding/COI extracted for every included study
sponsorship pattern checked across the body

nodes.definition: Move from certainty of evidence to recommendation strength (strong/conditional) using GRADE Evidence-to-Decision factors (benefits/harms, values, resources, equity, feasibility).
contradictors: panelist who equates high certainty with a strong recommendation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: values, resources, or certainty inputs change

pros.claim: EtD decouples strength from certainty, so high certainty can still yield a conditional recommendation
pros.example: strong evidence + close benefit-harm balance => conditional

pros.claim: Explicit values/equity/resource factors make the recommendation auditable
pros.example: resource cost downgrades to conditional

cons.claim: Conflating certainty with strength is the most common GRADE error
cons.example: 'high certainty so strong rec' shortcut

cons.claim: Values and resource inputs are often weak or absent
cons.example: no preference evidence forces panel judgment

failure_modes: mapping certainty directly to strength
omitting harms or equity from the EtD
acceptance_tests: strength derived from EtD factors not certainty alone
all EtD domains addressed or marked absent

nodes.definition: Run independent duplicate appraisal/grading and reconcile disagreements via documented adjudication to control assessor bias.
contradictors: single-assessor reviewer to save time

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: assessor judgments diverge beyond agreement threshold

pros.claim: Independent duplication and adjudication reduce single-assessor bias in every judgment
pros.example: two assessors catch a missed confounder

pros.claim: Documented reconciliation makes judgments defensible
pros.example: adjudication log shows how 'some concerns' was resolved

cons.claim: Doubles appraisal effort
cons.example: every RoB2/ROBINS-I done twice

cons.claim: Adjudication can entrench a dominant reviewer's view
cons.example: junior assessor defers to senior

failure_modes: consensus-by-discussion without independent first pass
no third-reviewer arbitration path

nodes.definition: Maintain a GRADE Evidence Profile that traces every certainty judgment to its domain rationale, source studies, and footnotes for audit.
contradictors: reviewer who reports ratings without rationale

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any domain rationale changes

pros.claim: Full domain-by-domain traceability makes every rating auditable and reproducible
pros.example: reviewer can reconstruct why 'low' was assigned

pros.claim: Versioned rationale supports updates and disputes
pros.example: tracks rating change after a new trial

cons.claim: Profiles are effortful to keep synchronized with evolving ratings
cons.example: footnotes drift from current judgments

cons.claim: Detail can overwhelm non-specialist readers
cons.example: Evidence Profile too dense for guideline users

failure_modes: ratings reported without domain rationale
footnotes not synchronized with current ratings
acceptance_tests: every certainty rating traces to its domain rationale and source studies
Evidence Profile complete for all critical outcomes

nodes.definition: Define triggers and procedures for re-grading certainty and re-appraising bias when new studies or evidence emerge after the initial appraisal.
contradictors: reviewer who treats a published grade as permanent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: surveillance finds a study that could change a rating

pros.claim: Defined re-grade triggers keep certainty ratings current for living guidelines
pros.example: a new large RCT triggers mortality re-grade

pros.claim: Impact analysis prevents wholesale re-grading when a study is immaterial
pros.example: low-weight study does not trigger update

cons.claim: Continuous surveillance is resource-intensive
cons.example: monthly searches for a living review

cons.claim: Update thresholds are judgment-based and can lag practice
cons.example: material study under-weighted, update delayed

failure_modes: no surveillance after publication
re-grading without impact analysis

nodes.definition: Govern which appraisal/grading tool versions and guidance editions are used so all judgments are consistent and reproducible across the review.

included: tool/version declaration (RoB2, ROBINS-I, AMSTAR-2, GRADE handbook edition)

contradictors: reviewer who mixes tool versions mid-review
inputs: available tool versions and guidance editions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a tool or guidance edition is revised mid-review

pros.claim: Declaring tool versions prevents silent inconsistency across appraisals
pros.example: whole review uses RoB2 v2019, not mixed with RoB1

pros.claim: Version lock makes the review reproducible and updatable
pros.example: reruns reproduce ratings under the declared edition

cons.claim: Locking to an old edition can miss improved guidance
cons.example: newer GRADE guidance not adopted

cons.claim: Version migration mid-review forces re-appraisal
cons.example: adopting RoB2 update means re-grading

failure_modes: mixing tool versions across studies
citing a guidance edition not actually used
acceptance_tests: one tool version declared per instrument
version lock recorded in the protocol

edges.why_related: Hierarchy mapping needs the frozen PICO and outcome set.
edges.example: Outcome list change re-anchors starting certainty.
edges.resolution_rule: scope dominates; re-run hierarchy on scope change

edges.why_related: RoB2 applies only after RCTs are classified.
edges.example: Trial labelled RCT then routed to RoB2.

edges.why_related: ROBINS-I applies only after NRSI are classified.
Tool selection depends on design classification.
Funding appraisal proceeds once studies are catalogued by design.
GRADE RoB domain aggregates RoB2 results.
GRADE RoB domain aggregates ROBINS-I results.
Upgrades evaluate NRSI only after ROBINS-I judgments exist.
edges.example: RR>2 cohort upgraded only if not serious.
edges.resolution_rule: no upgrade if serious downgrade remains

edges.why_related: Integration needs the RoB domain rating.
edges.example: RoB downgrade applied to net certainty.

edges.why_related: Integration needs the inconsistency rating.
Integration needs the indirectness rating.
Integration needs the imprecision rating.
Integration needs the publication-bias rating.
Integration applies upgrades after downgrades resolved.
SoF presents the integrated certainty per outcome.
Evidence Profile records the integration rationale.
Surveillance watches the finalized ratings for change.
EtD uses the SoF effects and certainty.
Indirectness compares studies to the frozen PICO.
CERQual relevance uses the review question.
Tool/version declaration follows protocol scope.
Reconciliation operates on duplicate RoB2 judgments.
Reconciliation operates on duplicate ROBINS-I judgments.
Sponsorship patterns change the probability of missing-study bias.
Funding can change the probability and direction of study-level bias.
Declared RoB2 version bounds how RCTs are appraised.
Declared GRADE edition bounds integration logic.
Reconciled RoB judgments change the aggregated RoB domain rating.
A complete Evidence Profile precedes defensible recommendations.
edges.example: Panel reads the profile before voting.

edges.why_related: Serious risk-of-bias pressure opposes any upgrade of the same evidence.
edges.resolution_rule: downgrade dominates; no upgrade while serious bias unresolved

edges.why_related: Pressure to equate high certainty with a strong recommendation conflicts with EtD-based strength.
edges.resolution_rule: EtD factors dominate; strength decoupled from certainty

edges.why_related: Imprecision and inconsistency can penalize the same sparse data twice.
edges.resolution_rule: attribute the dominant cause once; document

edges.why_related: Appraisal scores tempt substitution for the RoB certainty domain.
edges.resolution_rule: RoB tools dominate certainty; appraisal is contextual only

edges.why_related: New evidence pressures updates while version-lock resists tool changes.
edges.resolution_rule: update content under locked version unless migration approved

edges.why_related: Both are per-result, domain-based RoB tools for different designs.
edges.risk_of_conflict: Applying one tool to the wrong design.
edges.resolution_rule: route by design; do not interchange

edges.why_related: Both present GRADE certainty; profile is detailed, SoF is summary.
Relevance/applicability logic is analogous across quantitative and qualitative grading.
edges.resolution_rule: use the framework matched to evidence type

edges.why_related: Both probe reporting/sponsorship distortions of the body of evidence.

conflict_axes.trigger: panel infers recommendation strength directly from certainty level
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: EtD factors (values, resources, equity, balance) determine strength; certainty is one input only
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: disagreement persists after adjudication or affects a critical-outcome rating
conflict_axes.example: high certainty can yield a conditional recommendation when benefit-harm balance is close

conflict_axes.trigger: large-effect/dose-response present alongside serious risk of bias
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: no upgrade while any serious downgrade flag remains unresolved
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: disagreement persists after adjudication or affects a critical-outcome rating
conflict_axes.example: RR 6 cohort not upgraded because confounding domain is serious

conflict_axes.trigger: same sparse/flawed studies trigger penalties in multiple domains
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: attribute each concern to its dominant domain once; record attribution in the Evidence Profile
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: disagreement persists after adjudication or affects a critical-outcome rating
conflict_axes.example: few small heterogeneous high-RoB trials downgraded once, not three times

conflict_axes.trigger: appraisal checklist scores are reused as bias-certainty judgments
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: RoB2/ROBINS-I drive the certainty RoB domain; NOS/JBI/AMSTAR-2 are contextual only and never a certainty grade
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: disagreement persists after adjudication or affects a critical-outcome rating
conflict_axes.example: NOS 7/9 not converted into 'low risk of bias'

conflict_axes.trigger: duplicate per-result appraisal conflicts with rapid/living-review turnaround

workflow.objective: freeze PICO, prioritize outcomes, and declare tool/grading versions
workflow.do_first_because: scope and tool governance must precede all appraisal to prevent rework

workflow.objective: classify each study's design and set starting certainty anchors
workflow.do_first_because: starting anchors gate every up/down movement so they must be set early

workflow.objective: appraise risk of bias per result with dual independent assessors
workflow.do_first_because: risk of bias is the most labor-intensive input and must be reconciled before aggregation

workflow.objective: apply design-specific appraisal and funding/COI appraisal
acceptance_tests: each design mapped to one tool
workflow.do_first_because: quality and integrity context is needed before certainty-domain judgments

workflow.objective: judge the five GRADE downgrading domains per outcome
workflow.do_first_because: all downgrade domains must be settled before upgrades and integration

workflow.objective: apply upgrades and integrate to per-outcome overall certainty
acceptance_tests: no upgrade with unresolved serious downgrade
workflow.do_first_because: integration is the primary deliverable and gates all reporting

workflow.objective: assess CERQual confidence for any qualitative findings
acceptance_tests: each finding rated on all four components
workflow.do_first_because: qualitative confidence is independent and can run alongside quantitative grading

workflow.objective: build SoF tables and a complete Evidence Profile with traceable footnotes
acceptance_tests: each downgrade has a domain-linked footnote
exit_criteria: SoF and profile complete and synchronized
workflow.do_first_because: reporting must reflect finalized, traceable certainty before recommendations

workflow.objective: derive recommendation direction and strength via EtD factors
acceptance_tests: strength derived from EtD not certainty alone
workflow.do_first_because: recommendation is the final irreversible decision and requires human review before hard lock

workflow.objective: set re-grade triggers and surveillance for new evidence
workflow.do_first_because: surveillance keeps ratings current and reduces rework from late evidence
